generatedFrom: the branch as committed — no tenant was contacted
purpose: The primary register of every SharePoint list and Power Automate flow this branch holds any statement about, with the provenance of each statement and every conflict named rather than resolved.

evidenceBasis.tenant-observation: Read from the tenant. The only basis that evidences existence.
evidenceBasis.flow-definition: A flow definition reads or writes this column. Evidence a flow expects it, not that it exists.
evidenceBasis.client-code: The shipping client reads this column back. Evidence the client expects it.
evidenceBasis.specification: A specification declares it. Not evidence of existence.
evidenceBasis.generated-seed: Generated from configuration in this repository.

kinds.observed: read from the tenant on a stated date. The strongest claim available here.
kinds.specified: a design. Not evidence that anything exists.
kinds.derived: computed from other sources by a generator in this repository.
kinds.exported: a flow definition exported from Power Automate — authoritative about its own body.
kinds.superseded: kept for provenance. Never counted in a total.

identity.lists: A row keyed by GUID is a strong identity. A row keyed by site+title is weaker: 33 titles in this tenant name more than one list.
identity.flows: A flow has two identifiers in two spaces — a 36-character dashed Power Automate flow GUID and a 32-hex Logic Apps workflow id. GOV-06 measured the join and found ZERO of 77 exported definitions carrying an id the tenant register knows. Either field may be null. Neither is ever inferred from the other.

howToReadIt.whatIsNotHere: Current tenant state. Nothing here was read from the tenant at build time. The newest observation of the list estate is 2026-08-18; of the flow estate, 2026-09-26. Neither is today.
howToReadIt.tenantScope: The flow rows include every flow in the environment, not only this estate's. The 2026-09-26 export read 648 flows and classified 46 as used by this estate. Read totals.flows.byEstateUse before quoting any flow number.

fields.note: Only tenant-observation evidences existence. An earlier draft mapped internal-field-evidence's `deployed` to observed, which would have asserted 52 columns as seen on the tenant when that word means a flow definition writes to them.

flows.rowsAreUpperBound: A row is a distinct IDENTITY, not a proven distinct flow. Two rows may be one flow under two identifier spaces that GOV-06 proves do not resolve to each other. Use the bounds below.

inTheExportsOwnUnits.whyTheyDiffer: A register row is an identity, not a flow. Where two exported flows are pinned to one workflow id by two sources, both are recorded and one row carries both.

whatEachMeans.usedByThisEstate: The 2026-09-26 usage analysis names this flow as used, with its evidence, in at least one role.
whatEachMeans.inTheTenantExportAndNotEvidencedAsUsed: The export saw it in the environment and no evidence ties it to this estate. It is the tenant's, not necessarily Folio's.
whatEachMeans.notInTheTenantExport: No row in the 2026-09-26 export carries this identity. Either it is keyed on a workflow id the export does not carry — the export keys on the dashed flow id — or it is specified and not deployed.

knownDivergences.statement: Zero of the exported definitions carry an id the tenant register knows; 13 of 77 match on normalised display name.
knownDivergences.consequence: A flow row may exist twice in this register — once under each identifier space — and the register cannot merge them without fabricating the join.

knownDivergences.statement: The workbook extraction carries 97 field rows; the corrected table carries 98 (delta +1).
knownDivergences.consequence: Quoting one as "the" field count contradicts the other. The register uses the corrected table for field rows and reports both counts here.

knownDivergences.statement: The only tenant observation of the list estate is dated 2026-08-18.
knownDivergences.consequence: GOV-09 records rows written after it and GOV-11 records resources reported created after it. "Observed" here means observed then, not now.

knownDivergences.about: the two tenant readings of the flow estate
knownDivergences.statement: The 2026-09-18 Flow Management API reading covers 20 flows, requested by identifier. The 2026-09-26 "List My Flows" export covers 648. They are not the same population and neither supersedes the other: the first carries trigger authentication type per flow, which the second does not.
knownDivergences.consequence: A flow absent from the narrow reading is not absent from the tenant. A flow present in the wide export is not therefore this estate's. Rows carry both statements and the register merges neither.

knownDivergences.statement: The mailer declares 8 lists and 7 flows under contract dgo-mail/2.0, on https://nitdanigeria.sharepoint.com/sites/NITDADGO-EAAACTIVITYTRACKING. The tenant capture of 2026-08-18 predates the platform, so no source in this branch has observed any of them.
knownDivergences.consequence: Those rows are specified, not observed, however the platform behaves in service. The mailer's own setup provisions the lists on first run; nothing here evidences that it has.

statements.says: exists on DGO_ECM_GOVERNANCE as a List (Generic List) with null item(s)
required by the owner's 2026-09-24 decision: PROVISIONED
statements.decision: The internal platform and the Correspondence Gateway portal use SEPARATE proof ledgers. Taken by the platform owner on 2026-09-24, reversing an argument this repository made for sharing one list divided by a Purpose value.
statements.whyThatSite: Internal identity already lives there — DGO_UserDirectory and DGO_RoleCatalogue are on the governance site, and a session proof is an identity artefact. The portal's ledger stays where it is, on Global_Digital_Documents_Centre.
statements.whatIsBlocked: One value. scripts/build-identification-phase4.mjs reads listId from this file and uses it the moment it is set: the proof mint (OTP_VERIFY__IP_OTP_VERIFY__4dbe6dde) writes there and every identification package reads there. Until then they use the shared ledger and its internal-session Purpose filter, which is the arrangement this decision supersedes. A GUID cannot be invented here; a package naming a list that does not exist fails at run time. (The DGO_* generator that read this file before 2026-10-06 is retired.)
statements.untilThen: The internal flows read the portal's ledger filtered on Purpose eq 'internal-session', and every one of them carries that filter — npm run test:proofidentity asserts it on each. The separation holds today; it is one clause wide rather than structural, which is what this decision changes.

an index is required on RefIDD — Every single and bulk assignment resolves its target with `RefIDD eq`. 15,804 items at capture — already three times the view threshold, so this filter fails rather than slows. Open item 31.

an index is required on DueDate — DGO_SCHEDULED_SWEEP filters and sorts the due-date sweep on it. THIS ONE FAILED IN PRODUCTION: the first live run of AUTO_SCHEDULED_SWEEP returned status 400, 'exceeds the list view threshold', on Get_Due_Breached. Indexing is necessary and not sufficient — the sweep's query was also unbounded, and an indexed clause still has to return under 5,000 rows, which is why the flow now asks for a 30-day window rather than all history.
an index is required on Acknowledgement_x0020_Due_x0020_ — DGO_SCHEDULED_SWEEP filters and sorts the acknowledgement sweep on it. Failed in production alongside DueDate, same 400, same run.

an index is required on Modified — DGO_FETCH_ALL sorts the boot payload on it ($orderby Modified desc, $top 500). Past 5,000 items SharePoint refuses to SORT on an unindexed column exactly as it refuses to filter on one, so this is the same failure waiting for the boot call — latent only because the package is not pasted yet.

an index is required on AssignedTo — FETCH_ALL reads an officer's own tasks with `AssignedTo eq` (ITEM-90 role scoping, release 22): 16,071 items on 2026-10-08, so the filter needs the index. Live read 2026-10-08: AssignedTo is indexed.

a measured crossing by portal flow CG_Writeback_Endpoint: read — state ACCEPTED

record.appliesToEndpointsWhy: D16 accepts this crossing for all seven portal endpoints, and the seven designer-paste packages all carry it. The prose in `decision` and `reach` said so already; this states it in a form the boundary check can read, so a crossing appearing in a package that is NOT on this list fails the gate before anyone pastes it.
record.measuredBy: node scripts/verify-portal-wiring.mjs, against the deployed definition exported 2026-08-31
record.what: The deployed CG_Writeback_Endpoint reads its allowed CORS origins from Flow Configuration, which sits on the internal operations site. WRITEBACK is invoked by anonymous callers.
record.contradicts: This specification's own principle, verbatim: 'No portal flow may read or write the internal operations estate or any DGO_* governance list.' The read is of the internal operations estate. The principle admits no exception for reads.
record.reach: All seven portal designer-paste packages read the same list for the same value, so applying them extends this from one deployed endpoint to all seven. Seven internal packages and the ECM_DOCS_INTAKE bridge also read it, but those are tenant-authenticated and already inside the internal estate, so the principle does not speak to them.
record.whyItIsNotNothing: The value read is public by nature — an allowed origin is a scheme and a host that every response already announces in its own header. The risk is not the value, it is the connection: the flow's SharePoint connection is authorised against the internal operations site as a whole, not against one list, so any flaw that lets a caller influence what the flow reads reaches further than this one row. That is why the principle is stated absolutely rather than per-value.
record.whyItIsNotUrgent: Nothing reads back to the caller. The origin is used to populate a response header, the read is chained on all statuses and fails closed, and no portal response returns list content from this read.
record.decision: Accepted 2026-08-31 by the agency, recorded as D16. The value is public by nature, nothing from the read reaches the caller, the read fails closed, and the deployed endpoint already does this in production — so declining would leave six endpoints on older behaviour while the seventh kept crossing. Accepted for all seven portal endpoints, since all seven packages read the same list for the same value.
record.boundedTo: One list, one operation, one column: Flow Configuration, read, the ALLOWED_ORIGIN_* rows. Any other list, any write, or any read whose target a caller can influence is not covered and reopens the question. No secret is ever placed in this list.
record.reverses: Evidence that the read target can be influenced by a caller, or a decision to scope the portal flows' SharePoint connection to the portal estate — at which point moving the origins becomes the cheaper option.

record.purpose: Register a submission, mint its reference, and issue one upload ticket per declared attachment.

referenceMinting.mustNotUse: concat('NITDA-', yyyy, '-', last 3 digits of ticks(utcNow())) - the deployed expression. A thousand values per year drawn at random; a collision is more likely than not after about thirty-seven submissions.
referenceMinting.why: The legacy references are never persisted and no flow looks them up, so nothing depends on the old format. Minting sequentially from the counter, at a width the legacy form never used, keeps the two generations distinguishable to a person while both are in circulation during the deferred migration.

telemetry.where: Inside Scope_Flow_Data_Capture, alongside the existing Compose_Flow_Run_Record
telemetry.why: The house standard already composes the record in 23 flows and ships it by email. This gives it a queryable home. One create per run, in the capture scope, not on the request path.

record.requiredOperationsCorrection: A Portal Registry `update` was required here and is removed 2026-09-03. Nothing performs it and nothing needs to: Create_Submission_Record writes the COMPLETE row in one call — Title, ReferenceId, Subject, Category, CorrespondenceType, Channel, the five sender fields, EventDate, Description, AttachmentCount, SubmittedAtUtc, UpdatedAtUtc, Status, StatusLabel, ActionRequired, VerifiedSubmission, SourceIp and LocalId. The reference is minted BEFORE the create, so there is no second pass to write it back. Checked in all three places a create-then-update would have to appear: the deployed definition exported 2026-09-03, the Portal_SUBMISSION_ECM_DOCS paste package, and the 01-portal-submission design. None has one. Adding a no-op PatchItem to a live flow to satisfy a checklist would be worse than the gap it closed.

statements.says: the single sanctioned crossing: [object Object]

record.why: The single crossing between the public estate and the internal platform, and the only one. It is tenant-authenticated, read-only, and projects a fixed column set - so the portal estate can be written by anonymous callers without any of it becoming reachable from, or reaching into, the internal operations or governance estates.

writesBack.why: ECM_DOCS_INTAKE is a live read feed, not a copy, so a portal submission has no internal row to trigger on - the four flows that create in the internal estate never read Portal Registry. A trigger-based design would need a persistence path built first. Extending the crossing costs one flow edit and one config key, and keeps the number of crossings at one.
writesBack.backwardCompatible: Callers that send no action keep today's feed behaviour.

measuredState.what: ECM_DOCS_INTAKE (df7ddff1) does not exist in the tenant: the owner found no flow of that name (2026-10-08) and the Flow API answers 404 FlowNotFound. Its recorded definition was retired from contracts/deployed with it (registers/flow-retirement.json). Folio reads Portal Registry through IP_Dynamic_Global_Actions_Endpoint; where the staff status write-back runs is readiness ITEM-6, a decision.

previous.what: ECM_DOCS_INTAKE is present at workflow df7ddff1-9275-4f23-acf6-e169525f4e2f and performs its Portal Registry read. `npm run wiring` measures the crossing in place.

record.bearingOnD6: D6's one-crossing argument stands: the crossing exists and performs its read.
